newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Iraqi oil monitors still await U.N. all cleaR.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Iraqi oil monitors still await U.N. all cleaR.

text.p: Dutch industrial inspectors Saybolt, the company chosen by the United Nations to monitor Iraqi oil exports, is still awaiting instructions from the U.N. to send their full team to Iraq, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
"We are not going yet. We are ready to go. It is likely to be in the next few weeks, although we don't know for sure," the spokesman said.
Saybolt is due to place 14 inspectors on the ground in Iraq and in Turkey and on their border.

An advance team of three has already been working in Iraq and identified problems with a metering station on the Iraqi-Turkish border. They are expected to return to the Zakho station on December 5 to ensure the faulty equipment is operational.

Under the oil-for-food deal, signed between Iraq and the U.N. on May 20, Iraq is permitted to export $2 billion worth of oil over six months. Most will flow to the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan, with the rest heading to Mina-al-Bakr on Iraq's Gulf coast.
The plan was suspended by U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali in August after Iraq sent troops into northern Kurdish areas.
But Iraq said on Monday it now accepted U.N. terms for the deal.
